title: Sections are invariant under flat quasi-compact maps with connected geometric fibres
statement: Let $f:T\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] whose geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For every sheaf of sets $F$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], pullback induces a bijection $\Gamma(S,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,f^{-1}F)$, where $f^{-1}F$ is the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units].

proof.text: For each s, connectedness supplies a point x of the chosen geometric fibre. The pullback condition evaluated at x and Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply show that the first projection of x maps to s. This proves Surjective f in Lean. Apply Mathlib Scheme.Hom.singleton_mem_fpqcPrecoverage, using Flat f and QuasiCompact f, and Presieve.ofArrows_pUnit to obtain the PUnit-indexed fpqc cover.

For any section a upstairs, apply etaleSet_section_compatible_of_connected_geometricFibres to hconn, F and a. Its equality is definitionally the singleton hcompat hypothesis of existsUnique_etaleSection_of_fpqc_cover. Apply that existing descent theorem with the constant PUnit-indexed family to obtain a unique section downstairs for each upstairs section.

Let j be the canonical terminal-etale-object pullback lift, with inverse k the second projection. Prove j followed by k is identity using pullback.lift_snd; prove k followed by j is identity by pullback.hom_ext, pullback.lift_fst, pullback.lift_snd and pullback.condition. Thus restriction along j is bijective. The singleton descent conclusion says its composite with the original adjunction unit has unique preimages, so Function.bijective_iff_existsUnique makes that composite bijective. Cancel the bijective restriction by Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff\prime.
